title: LLM-based Optimization Algorithm Selection for High-Performance Networks Orchestration
problem: Network infrastructure for AI/LLM workloads is growing rapidly but cannot keep pace with demand, creating suboptimal resource utilization. Manual optimization of multi-domain, data-intensive networks is slow, error-prone, and unable to adapt to dynamic scenarios.
motivation: No universal optimization algorithm works across all network scenarios. Current manual processes cannot meet complex, multi-domain HPC network orchestration requirements. Need for automated, intelligent algorithm selection.
method: Proposes LLM-based framework for dynamic optimization algorithm selection. Uses LLM-generated embeddings of algorithms, network state logs, and service requests to identify optimal optimization method from pool of candidates. Framework triage matches scenario to algorithm.
key_novelty: LLM as meta-optimizer for algorithm selection in networks; embeddings capture algorithm behavior and network state; dynamic algorithm selection without hardcoded rules; preliminary framework for multi-domain orchestration.
contributions: Embedding-based representation of algorithms, network state, and service requests
Intelligent triage system matching scenarios to optimization methods
Framework design for multi-domain, high-performance network orchestration
limitations: Preliminary work (abstract states 'preliminary'); no empirical results provided; evaluation methodology not described; scalability to very large networks unclear; LLM accuracy not quantified
